results.notes: Australian since at least the 1920s (a 1927 Qld newspaper). The main recorded sense is very drunk; "stuffed with food" is the other. Old-timer flavour: younger speakers say "maggoted" or "smashed".

results.notes: "Root" is Australian slang for sex, so "rooted" (exhausted; broken) is impolite: vulgarity 2 is right. Never use "root" for US "root for (a team)"; Australians say "barrack for". "Get rooted" is a rude brush-off, a different sense.

results.notes: A shift of meaning, not a synonym. The fair go (fair treatment and an equal chance for everyone) is the closest Australian civic ideal to liberty.

args.text:
Now, Malia and Sasha, by the way, are stoked this is me last turkey pardon as President. What I haven't told 'em yet is we're gonna do this every year from now on. (Laughter.) No cameras. Just us. Every flamin' year. No way I'm givin' this habit up cold turkey. (Laughter and applause.)

Good one, that. Pretty funny, I reckon. (Laughter.)

Thanksgivin' is a chance -- (laughter) -- to get together with the people you love, count your blessings, and, after a campaign that dragged on longer than a wet week, finally take your eyes off the polls and put 'em on the poultry. This year we're chuffed to have two of the lucky ones here, raised by the Domino family out in Iowa: Tater and Tot.

Now, Tater's here on the bench, just in case Tot can't do the job on the day. So he's a bit like the Vice Turkey. We're tryin' to rustle him up a pair of aviator sunnies. (Laughter.)

And it's me great privilege -- well, it's me privilege -- actually, let's just say it's me job -- (laughter) -- to let 'em off the hook this arvo. While I'm at it, I wanna take a sec to tip me hat to the brave turkeys who weren't so lucky, who never got to ride the gravy train to freedom -- (laughter) -- who copped their fate with guts and sacrifice -- and proved they weren't chicken. Not a gutless chook among 'em. (Laughter.)

(Baby cries.)

THE PRESIDENT: Oh, it's not that bad, little fella. Come on now. (Laughter.)

Too bloody right we've got heaps to be thankful for this Thanksgivin'. Six straight years of new jobs -- the longest run ever. Unemployment's low. Wages are on the way up again. The gap between the haves and the have-nots is closin'. The housin' market's on the mend. The stock market's nearly tripled. Our high school graduation rate's at an all-time high. And the number of folks without health cover is at an all-time low, thanks to 20 million more Americans, millions of ankle biters among 'em, sticky fingers and all, who finally know they're covered if they get crook. (Applause.) Now that's worth a gobble or two. (Laughter.)

Proud families right across the country are finally complete now that marriage equality's the law of the land. And there's plenty of families of servicemen and women who've had an empty chair at the table these last few years, but this Thanksgivin' they can kick back with our brave troops and veterans, 'cause we've brought 'em home.

Thanksgivin's also a reminder of where we get our strength as a nation -- that out of many, we are one; that what holds us together isn't any one race or religion, but stickin' to a creed we all share, that all of us are created equal. And look, gettin' along with folks who aren't like you and buildin' a country with all sorts in it has never been easy, but it's never mattered more. We're a mob that looks out for each other and has each other's backs. We keep pushin' on, steered by values and ideals that've been a light for the whole of humanity.

We've gotta see ourselves in each other, 'cause we've all got families we love, and we all want somethin' better for 'em down the track. We lose sight of that sometimes, and Thanksgivin's a beaut time to remember it. We've got heaps more in common than what splits us.

The holidays are also when it matters even more to lend a hand to anyone who needs one. I reckon we're judged by how we look after the poor and the doin'-it-tough, the crook and the oldies, the immigrant, the refugee, every poor bugger who's after another crack at it. I believe that to really live up to those ideals we've gotta keep fightin' discrimination in every shape and form, and always show the world that America's a country that gives, and gives big.

We oughta make sure every man and his dog has a feed on Thanksgivin', too -- except the turkeys, of course, 'cause they're already stuffed. (Laughter.)

AUDIENCE: Ooooh --

THE PRESIDENT: (Laughter.) So, later today, the Obama family'll be pitchin' in on our usual Thanksgivin' service project. And when some bugger at your table tells ya you've been hoggin' all the sides and you're cut off, I hope ya come back at 'em with a creed that sums up the spirit of a hungry nation: Yes, We Cran. (Laughter.) That was a beaut. (Laughter.) Ya don't reckon that's funny? Look, I know there's a few stinkers in here, but this is the last time I'm doin' this, so we're not leavin' any room for leftovers. (Laughter.)

declined.reason: Wrong sense: 'working on getting him glasses' means trying to, not being ruined or exhausted.
Inverts the meaning: the turkeys who 'weren't so lucky' became 'a lucky bugger'.
'Of course' here is a transition, not agreement; and the f-word jars in a presidential speech with kids present. Used 'Too bloody right' instead.
Too flippant for children gaining health cover; used the riff 'ankle biters, sticky fingers and all' instead.
'Knocking together' implies something cobbled up cheaply; wrong for building a diverse society.
Wrong tone for a compassionate line about people needing a second chance; used 'every poor bugger'.
'A hungry people' means the nation at the table, not working-class strugglers; used 'a hungry nation'.
Breaks the 'Yes, We Can' pun in 'Yes, We Cran'.
